subtitle: Kailasanathar: When Pallava Stone Learned to Stand Forever

panels.shot: majestic low-angle wide of temple and king silhouetted against a dawn sky
panels.action: Narasimhavarman II Rajasimha stands in regal stillness before the rising mass of the Kailasanathar temple at Kanchipuram, stone tiers glowing in the first light.

dialogue.text: In Kanchipuram’s age of devotion, Rajasimha of the Pallavas raised Kailasanathar in stone, and changed the future of South Indian temples.

i18n.hi: भक्ति के युग में कांचीपुरम में, पालव राजसिंह ने पत्थर में कैलासनाथर उठाया, और दक्षिण के मंदिरों की दिशा बदल दी।

panels.shot: wide aerial view over Kanchipuram with temples and urban sprawl
panels.action: The camera floats over early medieval Kanchipuram, a sacred city of crowded streets, brick shrines and the distant shimmer of Mamallapuram’s shore, as Rajasimha surveys his capital from a terrace.

dialogue.text: By the late seventh century, Kanchipuram was a city of learning and worship, as the Pallava court watched Bhakti devotion rise like a new tide.

i18n.hi: सातवीं सदी के अंत तक, कांचीपुरम ज्ञान और पूजा का नगर था; पालव दरबार देख रहा था, भक्ति की लहर नई ज्वार की तरह चढ़ रही थी।

panels.shot: medium shot of the king examining palm-leaf manuscripts and plans
panels.action: Inside a pillared hall, Rajasimha sits attentive, palm-leaf texts and rough temple sketches laid before him, listening to architects and priests debate shrines, icons and sacred space.

dialogue.text: Rock-cut caves and monolithic rathas at Mamallapuram had tested Pallava skill, but the question now was bold: could devotion be housed in freestanding stone forever?

i18n.hi: मामल्लपुरम की गुफाएँ और एकाश्म रथ पालव कौशल आजमा चुके थे, पर अब सवाल था साहस का: क्या भक्ति को सदियों खड़ा रहने वाला स्वतंत्र पत्थर घर दे सकते हैं?

panels.shot: close-up on Rajasimha’s thoughtful face, lit by an oil lamp
panels.action: Rajasimha’s face is caught in flickering lamplight, eyes steady, jaw set, as he listens to talk of Shiva’s forms and the power of permanent royal shrines.

dialogue.speaker: narasimhavarman_ii_rajasimha
dialogue.text: Let Kanchi bear a stone Kailasa, where Shiva’s many forms dwell as one.

i18n.hi: कांची में उठे पत्थर का कैलास, जहाँ शिव के अनेक रूप एक रूप में बसें।

panels.shot: architectural bird’s-eye of the temple site with gridlines and stakes
panels.action: A leveled patch of earth outside the older city walls is marked in careful grids with stakes and strings, as Rajasimha watches master sthapatis trace a square around the future sanctum.

dialogue.text: On firm ground he ordered foundations laid, granite below for strength, carved sandstone above for grace, an experiment in structural stone.

i18n.hi: मजबूत ज़मीन पर नींव बिछी; नीचे शक्ति के लिए ग्रेनाइट, ऊपर शोभा के लिए नक्काशीदार बलुआ पत्थर—संरचनात्मक पत्थर का नया प्रयोग।

panels.shot: dynamic wide shot of quarry and workshop activity
panels.action: In a buzzing quarry-yard, huge granite blocks lie beside rows of pale sandstone; artisans measure, chisels poised, while messengers from the palace confer with foremen under a shade cloth.

dialogue.text: Stone moved in caravans from different sources, the heavier granite anchoring the base, the finer sandstone rising in sculpted stories toward the sky.

i18n.hi: पत्थर के काफिले अलग–अलग जगहों से चले; भारी ग्रेनाइट ने आधार थामा, महीन बलुआ पत्थर तराशी हुई कथाओं की तरह आसमान की ओर उठा।

panels.shot: low-angle view of sanctum core under construction, scaffolds rising
panels.action: A central cube of stone stands half-built, cloaked in bamboo scaffolds; workers climb and align blocks while Rajasimha looks up at the emerging tower like a mountain begun.

dialogue.text: At the heart rose the garbhagriha, the inner womb, wrapped by walls that would carry tiers of niches—each a chapter in Shiva’s vast story.

i18n.hi: बीच में उठा गर्भगृह, भीतरी कोख, चारों ओर दीवारें जिन पर कोटरों की परतें चढ़नी थीं—हर कोटर शिव–कथा का एक अध्याय।

panels.shot: close-up of sculptors chiseling Shaiva images on wall blocks
panels.action: Sculptors lean close to sandstone blocks, coaxing out dancing limbs, matted locks and tridents, as an overseer holds a palm-leaf list of Shaiva forms to be carved across the enclosure wall.

dialogue.text: Rajasimha’s temple would be an icon gallery: fierce, gentle, cosmic forms of Shiva lined along the prakara wall, a path of images for the circling devotee.

i18n.hi: राजसिंह का मंदिर बन रहा था मूर्तियों की दीर्घा—उग्र, कोमल, विराट शिव रूप प्राकार की दीवार पर सजे, परिक्रमा करते भक्त के लिए चित्रों की राह।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot of painters at work on fresh plaster
panels.action: Within a dim corridor, artists kneel before damp plaster, grinding pigments and laying fine lines—celestial figures and attendants—while a senior painter stands back to judge the composition.

dialogue.text: On newly plastered walls, painters added color to stone; their fragile murals tied Pallava Kanchi to wider currents of Indian sacred painting.

i18n.hi: ताज़ा गारे वाली दीवारों पर चित्रकारों ने पत्थर में रंग भरे; उनकी नाज़ुक भित्ति–चित्रों ने पालव कांची को भारत की व्यापक चित्र–भक्ति से जोड़ा।

panels.shot: medium shot of the king reading an inscription being carved
panels.action: By the temple’s entrance, an engraver bends over a stone slab, chiseling Tamil and Sanskrit while Rajasimha watches, one hand resting on the rough edge of the still-blank surface.

dialogue.text: Inscriptions on its stones named Rajasimha and his line, tying royal memory to the shrine of Kailasanathar and the merit of its making.

i18n.hi: पत्थरों पर खुदी लेखों में राजसिंह और उसका वंश दर्ज हुआ, राज–स्मृति को कैलासनाथर की देह और उसके पुण्य से बाँधते हुए।

panels.shot: solemn interior shot of near-complete sanctum with uninstalled linga
panels.action: Inside the quiet core sanctum, lit by a single shaft of light, a polished pedestal waits empty while priests and architects confer with Rajasimha at the threshold.

dialogue.speaker: narasimhavarman_ii_rajasimha
dialogue.text: When stone stands ready, Kailasanathar must be installed with all due rite.

i18n.hi: जब पत्थर तैयार खड़े हों, तब कैलासनाथर को पूरे विधि–विधान से प्रतिष्ठित करना ही होगा।

panels.shot: ceremonial wide shot of consecration with crowds and priests
panels.action: Under an awning bright with cloth, crowds of townsfolk, courtiers and ascetics gather as priests pour sacred water over a newly placed linga, with Rajasimha standing reverent near the doorway.

dialogue.text: When the linga was installed and consecrated, the royal experiment became a living temple, its stone now bound to ritual and song.

i18n.hi: जब लिंग स्थापित और अभिषिक्त हुआ, राज–प्रयोग जीवित मंदिर बन गया—पत्थर अब अनुष्ठान और गान से बंध गया।

panels.shot: tracking wide shot of devotees performing pradakshina along icon-lined wall
panels.action: Devotees of different ages walk barefoot along the outer passage, pausing before reliefs of Shiva as warrior, dancer, yogi, each niche catching lamplight and shadow.

dialogue.text: Along its walls, worshippers could meet Shiva in many moods, circled by stone images that invited meditation, awe and intimate prayer.

i18n.hi: दीवारों के सहारे भक्त शिव से कई मन–स्थितियों में मिल सकते थे; चारों ओर पत्थर–मूर्तियाँ थीं जो ध्यान, विस्मय और मन की गुप्त प्रार्थना को बुलाती थीं।

panels.shot: reflective medium shot of Rajasimha walking through the temple at dusk
panels.action: At dusk, Rajasimha walks alone through the pillared corridor, hand tracing a carved pilaster, his gaze lifting to the tower that now crowns the sanctum.

dialogue.text: For Rajasimha, Kailasanathar was both royal shrine and prototype, showing how structural stone could carry complex iconography and layered space.

i18n.hi: राजसिंह के लिए कैलासनाथर राज–देवालय भी था और नमूना भी, दिखाता हुआ कि संरचनात्मक पत्थर किस तरह जटिल मूर्ति–जगत और परतदार जगहें उठा सकता है।

panels.shot: paired wide shot showing Kailasanathar and a later-style temple silhouette beyond
panels.action: The composition frames Kailasanathar’s profile on one side and, in the hazy distance, the evolved silhouette of a later South Indian temple, echoing its tiers and enclosure.

dialogue.text: Later dynasties would build on Pallava experiments; Chola and others inherited the idea of stone temples with towering vimanas and articulated walls of gods.

i18n.hi: बाद की वंशावलियाँ पालव प्रयोगों पर आगे बढ़ीं; चोल और अन्य राजघराने ऊँचे विमान और देव–दीवारों वाले पत्थर मंदिरों की यही कल्पना विरासत में लेकर चले।

panels.shot: conservation-era interior shot with modern ASI worker studying faded paintings
panels.action: Centuries later, a modern conservator in simple clothes studies faint traces of mural on a temple wall, notebook in hand, lamplight revealing delicate lines on worn plaster.

dialogue.text: Our own age has traced its dates more closely and recorded its fading paintings, recognizing Kailasanathar as a precious link in India’s sacred art.

i18n.hi: हमारा समय उसके तिथियों को और साफ़ पढ़ चुका है, उसकी म्लान होती चित्रकारी दर्ज कर चुका है, कैलासनाथर को भारत की पावन कला की अमूल्य कड़ी मानते हुए।

panels.shot: final epic wide of Kailasanathar temple standing alone against the sky
panels.action: The Kailasanathar temple stands in serene completeness, enclosure, tower and shrines catching the sun, while visitors move small at its base and the sky stretches vast above.

dialogue.text: From granite roots to sculpted sandstone, Rajasimha’s Kailasanathar endures, proof that a single bold experiment in stone can shape a whole tradition of sacred building.

i18n.hi: ग्रेनाइट की जड़ों से तराशे बलुआ पत्थर तक, राजसिंह का कैलासनाथर आज भी अडिग है—सबूत कि पत्थर में एक साहसी प्रयोग पूरी पावन स्थापत्य परंपरा गढ़ सकता है।

subtitle_i18n.en: Kailasanathar: When Pallava Stone Learned to Stand Forever
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैलासनाथर: जब पालवों की पत्थर की देह सदा खड़ी रहना सीखी
